messages:
Alex: quick question — running into SIGTERM hang on our inference worker during deploys. Python service using opentelemetry-sdk + OTLP gRPC exporter. BatchSpanProcessor seems to block on shutdown. stack: gunicorn -> uvicorn workers. Anyone seen this pattern?
Maya: ugh yep. BatchSpanProcessor will try to flush pending spans; if exporter blocks it can hang. What versions?
Alex: otel 1.20.0, otlp-exporter 0.12. queue_size=4096, max_export_batch_size=512, schedule_delay_millis=200. We do a graceful_stop but sometimes processes still stuck 30s+ 
Sam: in Rust we had similar — background task not awaited during shutdown. We explicitly call provider.shutdown(ctx) with short timeout. In Python you can call tracer_provider.shutdown() but gunicorn/uvicorn signal handling complicates it.
Riley: for Go: always run tp.Shutdown(ctx) with 5s timeout in server.Stop(). For high-throughput inference I'd avoid relying on unbounded Batch flush during SIGTERM.
Maya: options: 1) reduce batch queue size and schedule so flushes happen more often 2) call force_flush with timeout in your signal handler 3) switch some spans to SimpleSpanProcessor for critical events so they are synchronous
Jamie: also consider collapsing token-generation into aggregated spans. Instead of creating span per-token, create one 'generation' span and set attributes: token_count, seq_len, model_version. That massively reduces queued spans.
Alex: good point — we do per-token spans for latency breakdowns. Maybe keep them in dev build only. But we still want per-request sampling to catch errors.
Maya: head-based sampling at ingress is good: sample 0.02 for regular, 1.0 for errors or traces with long latency. You can set sampling decision as an attribute propagated to children.
Sam: in Rust we tag spans with trace flags and use a ProbabilisticSampler on the SDK. For cross-lang consistency we should standardize the sampler config across libs.
Riley: exporter reliability: use OTLP over gRPC with retry/backoff and a bounded queue. Also route heavy inference traces to a cheaper pipeline with lower retention. No need to keep full spans for 90 days.
Jamie: correct — retention/cost tradeoff: keep detailed traces for 7 days, aggregated metrics for 90. Add a route in the collector that drops high-cardinality attributes before long-term storage.
Alex: collectors — are we ok relying on a shared agent or do we want per-region sidecars? We get bursts and the agent OOMs sometimes.
Maya: sidecars per node with resource limits + rate limiting at SDK side is safer. Also consider using an intermediate Kafka/ingest buffer for very high throughput before the collector.
Sam: implementation tasks: add cross-lang init helper that: sets resource attributes (service.name, deployment.environment, model.name), installs BatchSpanProcessor with sensible defaults, exposes force_flush and shutdown API, and documents sampling defaults.
Riley: +1. For Go and Rust, ensure shutdown is part of the server stop path. For Python add an atexit handler but also hook into gunicorn worker exit. Add an env var REDWOOD_OTEL_FORCE_FLUSH_TIMEOUT=3000ms.
Jamie: also add a small migration: change internal SDK to aggregate token spans behind a feature flag INFERENCE_AGG_SPANS so we can canary it.
Alex: sounds good. who wants to own the Python helper + docs? I can take it but will need examples for gunicorn + uvicorn.
Maya: I can pair on the docs and add Go/Rust snippets. Sam can do Rust helper. Riley can own Go. Jamie will add the rollout plan + feature flag.
ci-bot: created task INF-4827 "std otel init helpers + aggregation feature flag" and assigned to Alex, Maya, Sam, Riley, Jamie
Alex: thx — I'll open the PR with a simple helper: `init_otel(service, env, model, exporter_url, force_flush_ms=1000)` and a demo in examples/ with gunicorn hooks.
Maya: one more nit — track telemetry cost by model tag in Console so product can see which models burn trace budget. Add metrics for spans_emitted_per_model.
Jamie: action items summarized: create cross-lang helpers, implement aggregation feature flag, add graceful-shutdown examples, update retention routing in collector. We'll review in next platform sync.
Alex: perfect. I'll post the PR link when ready.
